entries.name: BTCPay Server
entries.use_for: Self-hosted Bitcoin and Lightning payment processor with no fees or intermediaries
entries.why: The standard self-hosted crypto payment gateway with e-commerce plugins and APIs
entries.summary: Free, self-hosted Bitcoin payment processor that lets merchants accept Bitcoin directly with no fees or intermediaries. It provides APIs (Greenfield), plugins and e-commerce integrations.
entries.best_for: Merchants or developers who want to accept Bitcoin and Lightning without a third-party processor, with their own server.
entries.not_for: You operate the server and wallet infrastructure yourself; crypto-only, not a card or fiat payments solution.

entries.name: dj-stripe
entries.use_for: Sync Stripe data into Django models and handle webhooks.
entries.why: Keeps a local copy of Stripe objects as Django models, simplifying queries and webhook handling.
entries.summary: Django package that implements Stripe models as Django models and keeps them in sync via a webhook endpoint. Covers Stripe core, Billing (subscriptions, invoices, prices), Payment Intents and multiple accounts.
entries.best_for: Django projects using Stripe Billing that want local queryable copies of customers, subscriptions and invoices.
entries.not_for: Django only and Stripe only; Stripe Connect support is partial. Adds many tables and tracks Stripe API versions, which adds upgrade work.

entries.name: Hyperswitch
entries.use_for: Route payments across many processors through one self-hostable API.
entries.why: Open-source payment orchestrator from Juspay: smart routing, retries and unified API for 50+ processors.
entries.summary: Open-source modular payments infrastructure that orchestrates payments across many processors via one API. Modules include smart routing, revenue recovery (retry strategies) and cost observability, and it is self-hostable.
entries.best_for: Businesses using multiple payment processors who want routing, retries and one integration, with control over their payment stack.
entries.not_for: Heavy to run for a single-processor shop; use the processor's own SDK instead. It is orchestration, not a processor itself.

entries.name: Kill Bill
entries.use_for: Run a self-hosted subscription billing and payments system.
entries.why: Mature, plugin-based billing platform in production for over a decade; Apache-2.0.
entries.summary: Open-source subscription billing and payments platform, in production since 2010. Handles catalogs, subscriptions, usage metering, invoicing, payments across gateways, credits, tax and dunning, with a modular plugin architecture.
entries.best_for: Running your own subscription billing engine with complex catalogs, trials and multiple gateways, owning the data.
entries.not_for: Java platform with significant ops footprint; overkill for a small SaaS where Stripe Billing suffices. Not all-in-one; plugins are needed for gateways and tax.

entries.name: Lago
entries.use_for: Meter usage and bill customers with usage-based or hybrid pricing.
entries.why: Leading open-source metering and billing API; self-host or cloud, integrates with Stripe and other gateways.
entries.summary: Open-source metering and billing system. Ingests usage events, turns them into billable metrics, applies pricing, credits and entitlements, then generates invoices and collects payments through gateways such as Stripe.
entries.best_for: Usage-based or hybrid pricing for AI and API products (tokens, compute, API calls), self-hosted or on Lago Cloud.
entries.not_for: Full platform to deploy and run; not needed for simple flat-fee subscriptions. Payment collection depends on integrated gateways.

entries.name: Laravel Cashier (Stripe)
entries.use_for: Add Stripe subscriptions, invoices and checkout to a Laravel app.
entries.why: Official Laravel package with a fluent API over Stripe Billing; the default choice for Laravel SaaS.
entries.summary: Official Laravel package giving a fluent interface to Stripe subscription billing. Handles coupons, plan swaps, subscription quantities, cancellation grace periods and invoice PDFs.
entries.best_for: Laravel apps selling subscriptions through Stripe.
entries.not_for: Laravel and Stripe only. For other processors or frameworks use a different library such as Omnipay or Pay for Rails.

entries.name: Omnipay
entries.use_for: Framework-agnostic multi-gateway payment library for PHP
entries.why: The standard PHP payments abstraction with many gateway drivers
entries.summary: Framework-agnostic multi-gateway payment library for PHP with a consistent API across gateway drivers. Includes unit tests and an example application.
entries.best_for: PHP projects that need to support several payment gateways or switch gateways without rewriting code.
entries.not_for: Lowest-common-denominator API may hide gateway-specific features; each gateway needs its own driver package of varying maintenance quality. PHP only.

entries.name: OpenMeter
entries.use_for: Collect and aggregate usage events (API calls, tokens) for billing and limits.
entries.why: Real-time metering built for AI/API products, with entitlements and Stripe sync.
entries.summary: Open-source monetization infrastructure for AI, API and usage-based products. Ingests CloudEvents, aggregates usage in real time, models plans and prices, calculates entitlements and handles subscriptions, credits and invoices, working with your existing payment and tax providers.
entries.best_for: Metering API calls or tokens per customer and enforcing usage limits or billing from usage, optionally syncing to Stripe.
entries.not_for: A multi-service platform to deploy; overkill for flat subscriptions. Payments and tax still come from external providers.

entries.name: Pay
entries.use_for: Add payments and subscriptions to a Ruby on Rails app with Stripe, Paddle or Braintree.
entries.why: Rails engine that unifies multiple processors behind one model API, including webhooks.
entries.summary: Payments engine for Ruby on Rails 6+ that puts several processors (Stripe, Paddle, Braintree and others) behind one model API, including webhook handling and subscription helpers.
entries.best_for: Rails apps that need subscriptions with Stripe, Paddle or Braintree and want ready-made models and webhooks.
entries.not_for: Rails only. A thin abstraction, so processor-specific features may need the processor's own gem; not for non-Rails stacks.

entries.name: Payum
entries.use_for: Integrate many payment gateways in PHP through one abstraction.
entries.why: Framework-agnostic PHP payment library with gateways for Stripe, PayPal and more; used by Sylius.
entries.summary: Framework-agnostic PHP payment library that integrates 50+ payment services behind one abstraction. Used by Sylius and friendly to major PHP frameworks.
entries.best_for: PHP projects (Symfony, Sylius, custom) integrating several gateways such as Stripe and PayPal through a single API.
entries.not_for: PHP only. The README is thin and the abstraction is fairly heavy; for a single gateway the official SDK is simpler.

entries.name: Polar
entries.use_for: Sell subscriptions and digital products with a merchant-of-record handling tax.
entries.why: Open-source billing platform with SDKs and framework adapters; handles global sales tax as MoR.
entries.summary: Open-source billing platform for software and AI products, built around usage billing, subscriptions, seats, credits, trials and discounts. Acts as a merchant of record handling global sales tax, with SDKs and framework adapters.
entries.best_for: Indie developers and AI startups selling subscriptions, digital products or usage-based plans who want tax handled for them.
entries.not_for: You depend on Polar as merchant of record and its fees; not for owning the payment stack or for physical goods. Self-hosting is a heavy option.

entries.name: react-native-iap (OpenIAP)
entries.use_for: In-app purchases and subscriptions for React Native/Expo on iOS and Android
entries.why: Home of react-native-iap (moved from hyochan/react-native-iap); the most used open-source IAP library for React Native
entries.summary: Home of the OpenIAP protocols: a Client Protocol for a unified in-app purchase API across stores and a Commerce Protocol for backend verification and entitlements. Also hosts react-native-iap, the open-source IAP library for React Native.
entries.best_for: React Native or Expo apps that need in-app purchases and subscriptions on iOS and Android without a paid third-party service.
entries.not_for: You handle receipt validation and entitlements yourself unless you add a backend; RevenueCat offers a managed alternative.

entries.name: RevenueCat React Native
entries.use_for: Add in-app purchases and subscriptions to iOS/Android React Native apps.
entries.why: Official RevenueCat SDK abstracting StoreKit and Google Play Billing with receipt validation.
entries.summary: Official RevenueCat SDK for React Native. Wraps StoreKit, Google Play Billing and RevenueCat Web Billing to fetch products, make purchases and check subscription status, backed by RevenueCat's hosted server.
entries.best_for: React Native apps wanting subscriptions with server-side receipt validation, remote product config, analytics and webhooks handled for you.
entries.not_for: Requires a RevenueCat account and backend (free tier, then revenue-based pricing); not usable standalone for pure DIY IAP.

entries.name: Stripe Agent Toolkit
entries.use_for: Let LLM agents use Stripe through function calling, MCP and agent frameworks
entries.why: Official Stripe toolkit for OpenAI, LangChain, Vercel AI SDK and MCP agents
entries.summary: Official Stripe repo of SDKs for building AI products on Stripe, including @stripe/ai-sdk for the Vercel AI SDK and @stripe/token-meter for metering OpenAI, Anthropic and Gemini usage into Stripe billing, plus agent toolkit and MCP support.
entries.best_for: Letting LLM agents call Stripe tools or billing AI token usage through Stripe in Vercel AI SDK or native-SDK apps.
entries.not_for: Stripe only and mostly JS/TS-focused; not a general payment SDK. Agents with Stripe write access need careful permission scoping.

entries.name: Stripe CLI
entries.use_for: Test webhooks locally, trigger events and call the Stripe API from the terminal
entries.why: Official tool for forwarding webhooks to localhost and triggering test events
entries.summary: Official Stripe command-line tool to build, test and manage integrations. Forwards webhooks to localhost, triggers or resends test events, tails API request logs and creates or updates API objects from the terminal.
entries.best_for: Local development and testing of Stripe webhooks, triggering test events and quick API calls.
entries.not_for: A development tool, not a library to ship in your app; only works with Stripe.

entries.name: Stripe Node.js
entries.use_for: Call the Stripe API (payments, subscriptions, webhooks) from Node.js.
entries.why: Official, typed Stripe SDK for Node, kept in step with Stripe API versions.
entries.summary: Official typed Stripe SDK for server-side JavaScript. Provides access to the Stripe API (customers, payments, subscriptions, webhooks) and is kept in step with Stripe API versions.
entries.best_for: Node.js or TypeScript backends calling the Stripe API.
entries.not_for: Server-side only; use Stripe.js (stripe-js) for collecting card details in the browser. Stripe only.

entries.name: Stripe PHP
entries.use_for: Official PHP library for the Stripe API
entries.why: Official, actively maintained Stripe SDK for PHP backends
entries.summary: Official Stripe PHP library providing classes for API resources that initialize from API responses. Supports a StripeClient service pattern as well as legacy static patterns.
entries.best_for: PHP backends (Laravel, Symfony, plain PHP) integrating with the Stripe API.
entries.not_for: Stripe only and server-side; for Laravel subscription conveniences consider Cashier on top.

entries.name: Stripe Python
entries.use_for: Call the Stripe API from Python backends.
entries.why: Official Stripe SDK for Python with typed resources and async support.
entries.summary: Official Stripe SDK for Python with typed API resources and a StripeClient class (introduced in v8) alongside a legacy module-level pattern, including async support.
entries.best_for: Python backends such as Django, Flask or FastAPI calling the Stripe API.
entries.not_for: Stripe only and server-side; Django users wanting local models may add dj-stripe. Legacy and client patterns coexist, so pick one.

entries.name: Stripe.js
entries.use_for: Load Stripe.js and use Elements and Checkout in the browser with TypeScript types
entries.why: Official browser loader for Stripe Elements/Checkout; pairs with stripe-node
entries.summary: Official ES/CommonJS wrapper that loads Stripe.js from js.stripe.com via loadStripe and provides TypeScript types for Elements and Checkout. Stripe.js itself must be loaded from Stripe for PCI compliance.
entries.best_for: Frontend apps in any bundler setup that collect payments with Stripe Elements or Checkout and want typed APIs.
entries.not_for: Cannot bundle or self-host Stripe.js (PCI requirement); front-end only and requires a backend such as stripe-node for secrets.
